implementation.note: Metal pixel tests cover model alpha/weighted/unweighted and display-particle sprite/mesh/trail/ribbon/graph, depth, fog and resize. Actual Metal/WebGL three-scene demo confirms host integration. Final integrated test gate tracked separately.

architecture.note: ParticleSystem records already-uploaded geometry, Renderer3D invokes a generic display callback after existing PRISMA resolve with original depth. Consumers call renderScene; no genre-specific compositor or alternate tone mapping owner.

native_api.note: Public FxBlendSpace, renderScene and renderDisplay use existing ParticleSystem/Renderer3D lifetime and view. Real native fixture covers display geometry/depth/fog/resize; upload is reused through resolve.

skill.note: Existing owner recipe documents exact authoring route, shared semantics, example and verified backend limits.

performance.note: Scoped macOS Debug/Rosetta acceptance: three480-frame scenes plus two720-frame linear/display loads (expected1024particles). Post-warmup CPU block means below16.67ms, sampled completed GPU frames below16.67ms and process peakRSS below512MiB. Allocation review records reusable particle buffers and recurring callback-list allocation; no zero-allocation, p95, leak or cross-device claim.

platforms.note: Verified scope: native macOS Metal and Emscripten browser WebGL runtime, using retained real captures. Windows, Linux desktop and physical mobile devices are NOT RUN; these results do not establish their backend/runtime parity.

dependencies.note: Uses existing gfx blend state, Renderer3D, model/particle owners and PRISMA resolve. No package or competing rendering pipeline added.

headless.note: Presentation blend state only; no server simulation or authoritative gameplay state is introduced. Parsing remains ordinary data code.

examples.note: Three ordinary material-effects scenes verified in actual Metal and WebGL captures: shadow switch, weighted/unweighted model addition, linear/display particles. No special demo runtime path. Publication pending.
